To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the monodromies of the fundamental solutions of the linear system associated with a symmetry-reduced Einstein equation are completely determined by the characteristic initial conditions for the reduced Einstein field equations, and (2) the solutions of the symmetry-reduced field equations are expressed in quadrature in terms of the solutions of the linear Fredholm integral equations for the scattering matrices.

the symmetry-reduced field equations can be written as linear integral equations for the field components in terms of a new set of evolving monodromy parameters, that the characteristic initial data uniquely determine these parameters, and that the field components are expressed quadratically in terms of solutions to the new integral equations.

the symmetry-reduced field components are expressed as solutions of linear (quasifredholm) integral (or integro-differential) equations that are equivalent, in the sense of functional analysis, to the symmetry-reductions of the Einstein equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic analysis of integrable reductions of Einstein’s equations in the form of linear systems with spectral parameter.

the construction of new classes of solutions to the Einstein equations in vacuum and with the development of a new approach to solving the Goursat and Cauchy problems in terms of the monodromies of the linear systems associated with the Einstein equations.
the construction of integrable reductions of Einstein's field equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the monodrominess of the fundamental solutions of the linear systems of differential equations associated with integrable reductions of Einstein’s equations is a powerful tool for constructing the most general solutions of the symmetry-reduced field equations.

, in the present work, we have established a new method for the solution of the symmetry-reduced hyperbolic and the elliptic Einstein equations, and we have demonstrated that it is equivalent to the monodromymethod of the present authors and of the authors of Ref. 1.

the integral representation of the solutions of the symmetry-reduced equations in terms of the dynamic monodromy matrix is a very powerful method for constructing the solutions of the Einstein equations in terms of quadratures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monodromies of the fundamental solutions of the linear systems associated with integrable reductions of Einstein equations provide a complete and consistent description of the solutions in terms of the characteristic data.

we have constructed a new class of integral representations of the Einstein equations, which are integrable and can be used to solve the Einstein equations for hyperbolic and, in principle, for elliptic reductions.
the new integral equations provide a new approach to the Goursat (Cauchy-Kowalewski) problem for the symmetry-reduced field equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integral equation form of integrable reductions of hyperbolic and/or elliptic equations of mathematical physics is not unique and can be obtained in different equivalent ways.
the monodromic data of scattering matrices are a natural generalization of the monodromicity of the corresponding fundamental solutions.

the monodromic structure of the linear system for the fundamental solution of the associated hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein equations can be used to construct a new class of integrable reductions that can be analyzed in a more direct and systematic way.
